facts.text: The Eiffel Tower in Paris was completed in 1889 for the World's Fair.
The Statue of Liberty was dedicated on October 28, 1886, a gift from France to the United States.
Major construction of the Great Wall of China happened under the Ming Dynasty, primarily between 1368 and 1644.
The Taj Mahal in Agra, India was completed in 1653 under the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan.
The Sydney Opera House opened on October 20, 1973.
Charles Darwin, the English naturalist, was born on February 12, 1809.
Albert Einstein, the physicist who developed relativity, was born on March 14, 1879.
Marie Curie, the Polish-French physicist and chemist, was born on November 7, 1867.
Ada Lovelace, often called the first computer programmer, was born on December 10, 1815.
Isaac Newton, the English mathematician and physicist, was born on January 4, 1643.
William Shakespeare, the English playwright, was born on April 23, 1564 in Stratford-upon-Avon.
Nikola Tesla, the Serbian-American inventor, was born on July 10, 1856.
Apollo 11 landed on the moon on July 20, 1969, with Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walking on the surface.
The Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989.
Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite, was launched by the Soviet Union on October 4, 1957.
The Wright brothers made the first powered flight on December 17, 1903 at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.
World War I ended on November 11, 1918 with the Armistice.
World War II in Europe ended on May 8, 1945, known as V-E Day.
Mount Everest is the highest mountain on Earth, with a peak at 8,849 meters (29,032 feet) above sea level.
Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is 5,895 meters (19,341 feet) high, the highest peak in Africa.
The Nile River is approximately 6,650 kilometers long, traditionally considered the longest river in the world.
The Amazon River in South America is approximately 6,400 kilometers long.
Tokyo, the capital of Japan, has a metropolitan area population of approximately 37 million people, the largest in the world.
Delhi, the capital region of India, has a metropolitan area population of approximately 32 million people.
The speed of light in a vacuum is 299,792,458 meters per second, or approximately 300,000 kilometers per second.
The circumference of the Earth at the equator is approximately 40,075 kilometers.
William Shakespeare wrote Hamlet around 1600-1601.
Charles Darwin published On the Origin of Species on November 24, 1859.
Albert Einstein published his special theory of relativity in 1905, during his 'miracle year' (annus mirabilis).
Isaac Newton published his Principia Mathematica in 1687.
